title: Real-Hardware Deployment of a Nussbaum-Function PID Controller on a Current-Controlled Low-Cost Actuator via Hardware-Aware Optuna Tuning
authors: Danial Zafaranchizadeh Moghaddam; Olga Tveretina; Abolfazl Zaraki
locator: Design, final parameters and Sec. 4; Tables 4–6; data availability; data/README.md in pinned author archive
finding: Two command definitions matter: internal u clamp for tracking trials, raw-current proximity in the Optuna objective. Paper equations 12/18 and the released final configuration reproduce all 7,200 clipped internal commands; 82 exceed the cap before clipping. The public archive exposes measured onboard current and selected high-penalty trials. No separate shaft-torque channel in the 16 distinct logs.
rights: Publisher article CC BY 4.0. Original annotations and derived results.

title: A Novel Tribometer and a Comprehensive Testing Method for Rolling-Sliding Conditions
authors: Pedro Amoroso; Aleks Vrček; Matthijn de Rooij
locator: Sections 3–4, test apparatus, torque-mode traction and traction-decay tests, Figs. 12–17
finding: Torque sensor closes the hysteresis-brake loop; the flexure-mounted load cell independently measures traction. The braking sensor excludes bearing friction. At steady speed, comparing tangential force times roller radius to measured braking torque resolves this distinction.
rights: CC BY 4.0 for the article; dataset has separate CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 terms.

title: Direct current geared motor data: Voltage, current, and speed measured under different experimental conditions
authors: Wallace Pereira Neves dos Reis; Giselle Elias Couto; Orides Morandin Junior
locator: Experimental design, Table 1, voltage and current calibration and data description
finding: The PWM output reference, measured terminal potential difference, Hall-based current and motor speed are separate channels. These are command-response identification/excitation tests; the dataset does not record pre-clamp demand or measured shaft torque.
rights: Published CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; source links and independent descriptions only.

title: “CREATOR case”: PMSM and IM electric machine data for validation and benchmarking of simulation and modeling approaches
authors: Annette Muetze; Kourosh Heidarikani; Pawan Kumar Dhakal; Roland Seebacher; Sebastian Schöps
locator: Deposited author version, Secs. 5.2.3/6.2.3 and references Heidarikani and Dhakal (2024)
finding: Companion original study for the paired motor families. Here the induction-machine archive supplies torque/speed reference and measured power arrays on common time grids. The study family also has a separate previously catalogued PMSM release.
rights: Author-version source and bibliographic citation only. Data package CC BY-NC 4.0.

title: Soft Disagreement-Based Adaptive Uncertainty Regulation for Fuzzy Servo Control
authors: Dosti Kheder Abbas; Sadegh Abdollah Aminifar
locator: Section 3.1 and data availability; accompanying release description
finding: Six operating regimes in an industrial Delta servo drive are represented as post-processed feature vectors. This evidence addresses classification of labelled regimes. It cannot yield the time fraction of actual actuator clipping.

authors: Yukinori Inoue; Shigeo Morimoto; Masayuki Sanada

title: Hybrid physics-informed and data-driven model for torque estimation—toward real-time sensorless control of ultrasonic motors
authors: Yanbo Wang; Chuhang Lin; Zhirui Chen; Tatsuki Sasamura; Takeshi Morita
locator: Publisher article summary and indexed Sec. 4.1
finding: Ultrasonic-motor torque estimation has a separate shaft torque sensor, monitored current components, vibration amplitude and internal operating temperature. Full open raw data stream not verified in this pass.

title: Closing the Loop on Exoskeleton Motor Controllers: Benefits of Regression-Based Open-Loop Control
authors: Greg Orekhov; Jason Luque; Zachary F. Lerner
locator: Author manuscript Secs. II.A/B, Fig. 1 and treadmill results
finding: An encoder/current channel and independent ankle torque sensor allow tracking comparisons. With five participants, the reported comparison of RMS tracking error between closed/open-loop controllers yielded p=0.23. Separate torque-limiter input/output and raw file release not verified.
rights: Public author manuscript; original annotations, no figure or human measurement rows redistributed.

title: Comparing the Electrical Modeling and Thermal Analysis Toolbox Simulation Data to Electrified Aircraft Propulsion Test Hardware Data
authors: Mark E. Bell; Santino J. Bianco; Jonathan S. Litt
locator: NASA technical memorandum, p. 7, Table 2 and Fig. 6 footnotes
finding: Two back-to-back machines switch speed/torque roles. The external torque transducer samples every 50 µs and was decimated by 300 to match the 15 ms inverter telemetry. The unfiltered transducer fluctuates up to about ±15 N·m. Table 2 specifies 80 nominal setpoints. No separate open per-event hardware file identified.
rights: NASA-hosted public technical report with contractor coauthorship. Original citations and summary only.
